paper_metadata.title: Quantum Architecture Search for Quantum Monte Carlo Integration via Conditional Parameterized Circuits with Application to Finance

experiments.description: Genetically trained PQC and its conditional variant for approximating the payoff of a European call option, compared against a bitwise quantum arithmetic baseline across varying control-qubit counts.

algorithm.variant: Genetic structure learning for PQC/CPQC payoff approximation
algorithm.ansatz: Custom PQC with alternating encoding and parameterized blocks; encoding blocks use single-qubit rotations (RX, RY, RZ)
algorithm.optimizer: PennyLane RMSProp for parameter optimization; genetic selection/mutation for structure search
algorithm.convergence_criteria: 20 generations; 20 structure-optimization iterations per generation; accept new structure if cost decreases, or with probability exp(-5(cnew-cold)/cold) if cost increases

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Asset price x discretized on n control qubits; basis encoding used in CPQC control register; PQC uses rotational encodings of x
problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate European call payoff f+(X)=max(X-K,0) via quantum model output

problem_instance.description: European vanilla call option payoff approximation with strike K=100

dataset_specification.description: Discretized asset prices shown in Fig. 3/4; exact training set size not explicitly stated beyond the plotted discretization

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Scaled discretization xk in [0,2π) with bit representation b(xk)
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Function approximation visualized against true payoff; scalability comparison of CNOT count and depth versus bitwise quantum arithmetic across control-qubit counts

noise_model.noise_description: none reported; noiseless simulator used for gradients

implementation_details.transpilation_target: CNOT and U(θ,φ,λ) decomposition for resource comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical pretraining of PQC structure and parameters on training data
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Discount expected payoff classically to obtain option price

classical_baselines.method_name: ibm qiskit finance bitwise quantum arithmetic
ibm qiskit finance bitwise quantum arithmetic

speedup_claims.conditions: assuming amplitude estimation and efficient implementation of the function oracle
speedup_claims.caveats: The quadratic speedup is in the number of simulations; practical advantage depends on efficient state preparation and function implementation.

speedup_claims.factor: lower cnot count and depth than bitwise quantum arithmetic
speedup_claims.baseline_method: ibm qiskit finance bitwise quantum arithmetic
speedup_claims.conditions: for the reported European call option resource comparison
speedup_claims.caveats: Exact baseline counts are shown only in the figure; the paper states the CPQC has fewer resources and reports 92 CNOTs and depth 151 for n=14.

experiments.description: Genetically trained PQC and its conditional variant for approximating the payoff of a European basket option with fixed weights, compared against a bitwise quantum arithmetic baseline across varying control-qubit counts.

algorithm.variant: Genetic structure learning for PQC/CPQC basket payoff approximation with fixed weights
algorithm.ansatz: Custom PQC with rotational encodings and parameterized blocks; CPQC built from controlled rotations
algorithm.optimizer: PennyLane RMSProp for parameter optimization; genetic selection/mutation for structure search
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Same genetic procedure as the call-option experiment; 20 generations and 20 iterations per generation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two underlyings X(1), X(2) each discretized on separate qubit registers; CPQC uses basis-encoded control registers and controlled rotations
problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate basket payoff fBasket(X)=max(wX-K,0) with fixed weights w=(2/3,1/3)

problem_instance.description: European basket call option with two underlyings and fixed weights

dataset_specification.description: Two-asset basket; discretization sizes varied via control-qubit count n, with nk=n/2 per asset in the comparison plot

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Scaled discretization of each underlying into basis states; same discretization resolution required for the quantum arithmetic baseline
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Function approximation compared to true payoff; resource scaling compared to IBM qiskit finance bitwise implementation; for n=14, CPQC reported CNOT count 92 and depth 151

noise_model.noise_description: none reported; noiseless simulator used for gradients

implementation_details.transpilation_target: CNOT and U(θ,φ,λ) decomposition for resource comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical pretraining of PQC structure and parameters on training data
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Discount expected payoff classically to obtain option price

classical_baselines.method_name: ibm qiskit finance bitwise quantum arithmetic
ibm qiskit finance bitwise quantum arithmetic

speedup_claims.conditions: assuming amplitude estimation and efficient implementation of the function oracle
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper emphasizes that the quantum arithmetic baseline scales as O(n log n) while the CPQC scales as O(n) in control-qubit count for a fixed approximation level.

speedup_claims.factor: lower cnot count and depth than bitwise quantum arithmetic
speedup_claims.baseline_method: ibm qiskit finance bitwise quantum arithmetic
speedup_claims.conditions: for the reported basket option resource comparison
speedup_claims.caveats: Exact baseline counts are not numerically listed in the text; the comparison is shown in Fig. 6. The paper reports CPQC has 92 CNOTs and depth 151 at n=14.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: quantum arithmetic implementation of basket option pricing
speedup_claims.conditions: for fixed approximation level and increasing control-qubit count
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a scaling claim derived from the circuit construction, not a formal runtime benchmark.

experiments.description: Genetically trained PQC and its conditional variant for approximating a European basket option with variable weight as an input feature.

algorithm.variant: Genetic structure learning for PQC/CPQC basket payoff approximation with variable weight input
algorithm.ansatz: Custom PQC with one-time encoding of variable weight and rotational data encodings; CPQC constructed from controlled rotations
algorithm.optimizer: Not explicitly stated for this specific experiment; same genetic/PennyLane-based procedure as the other PQC experiments

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Three inputs: two asset values and the first asset weight; weight w1 encoded once at the start of the circuit
problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate basket payoff with variable weight, effectively learning a rotated payoff surface

problem_instance.description: European basket call option with variable weight

dataset_specification.description: Two underlyings plus variable weight w1; figure shows three example weights w1=0, w1≈0.37, w1≈0.74

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Scaled discretization of asset values and weight into rotational encodings
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Qualitative comparison of predicted payoff surface against true payoff for multiple weight settings

noise_model.noise_description: none reported; noiseless simulator used for gradients

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical pretraining of PQC structure and parameters on training data
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: No explicit postprocessing beyond visual comparison to the true payoff surface

speedup_claims.caveats: No quantitative classical baseline or speedup comparison is reported for the variable-weight basket option; the result is presented qualitatively.
